dedupe_keys.name: project ukko interactive visualisation of seasonal wind speed predictions for the energy sector euporias resilience prototype

description: Project Ukko is an interactive climate service interface for wind industry users to explore probabilistic wind speed predictions for the coming season. It was built by FutureEverything and the Barcelona Supercomputing Center for the EUPORIAS project, funded by EU FP7, with data visualisation by Moritz Stefaner. The predictions come from the RESILIENCE prototype, which uses 10-metre wind speed forecasts from the ECMWF System 4 seasonal prediction system, validated against ERA-Interim surface wind; the background page explains that model biases need correction. The aim is to help traders, wind farm managers and others understand wind resource variability over the next few months, not relying only on retrospective climatology. The viewer is freely available online with no sign-in, alongside a summary video and background documentation, and Climate-ADAPT lists it as a tool under storms for the energy sector, last modified in 2023. Coverage is global. Caveats: the prototype dates from the EUPORIAS project era, no licence or data download is offered, and the viewer is a visualisation, not a dataset. Simulation uses are seasonal wind resource outlooks as context for power system operations and planning. Related records: data-era5-cutouts-pypsa-eur-1980-2020 gives historical wind inputs.
